borderlineBooks.title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
borderlineBooks.reason: Gothic aestheticism classic that bridges philosophical literary fiction and supernatural gothic horror.

borderlineBooks.title: House of Leaves
borderlineBooks.reason: Ergodic postmodern novel combining psychological terror, academic satire, and unconventional literary fiction.

borderlineBooks.title: Frankenstein
borderlineBooks.reason: Widely recognized as both the foundational pioneer of science fiction and a gothic horror classic; assigned all three canonical genres to maximize discoverability.

borderlineBooks.title: The Silence of the Lambs
borderlineBooks.reason: Frequently debated between psychological horror vs. forensic crime thriller; categorized here primarily under thriller and crime.

borderlineBooks.title: The Road
borderlineBooks.reason: Post-apocalyptic desolate journey; classified under dystopian and literary fiction rather than technology-driven science fiction.

borderlineBooks.title: Station Eleven
borderlineBooks.reason: Post-pandemic civilization collapse focusing on Shakespearean art and human memory; classified as dystopian and literary fiction.

borderlineBooks.title: Harrow the Ninth
borderlineBooks.reason: Science-fantasy space necromancy hybrid blending high magic, dark fantasy atmosphere, and interstellar science fiction.

borderlineBooks.title: The Underground Railroad
borderlineBooks.reason: Historical antebellum narrative employing a literal physical underground train system, introducing magical realism elements.

borderlineBooks.title: A Canticle for Leibowitz
borderlineBooks.reason: Post-nuclear multi-century saga bridging monastic theology, dark satire, and speculative science fiction.

borderlineBooks.title: All Quiet on the Western Front
borderlineBooks.reason: Semi-autobiographical World War I account published as fiction; canonized as a 20th-century historical fiction classic.

borderlineBooks.title: The Book Thief
borderlineBooks.reason: Narrated by Death in Nazi Germany; often marketed to Young Adults, but classified here under historical fiction and literary fiction.

borderlineBooks.title: Lamb: The Gospel According to Biff, Christ's Childhood Pal
borderlineBooks.reason: A comic retelling of Jesus's hidden years blending humor, satire, and religion & spirituality.

borderlineBooks.title: Moneyball
borderlineBooks.reason: Examines baseball player valuation and market inefficiency; classified under business rather than general economics.

borderlineBooks.title: On the Road
borderlineBooks.reason: A defining novel of the Beat Generation; road trip travel serves as the narrative backdrop rather than a nonfiction travelogue.
